paper_title: RLPlanner: Reinforcement Learning based Floorplanning for Chiplets with Fast Thermal Analysis

scenario.description: Multi-GPU System benchmark from reference [4]: RLPlanner floorplanning optimization comparing wirelength, maximum temperature, and runtime against TAP-2.5D baseline with HotSpot thermal solver
scenario.architecture: Chiplet-based multi-GPU system with 2.5D integration and interposer
scenario.operating_point: Maximum operating temperature: 91.15 °C (RLPlanner) vs 91.68 °C (TAP-2.5D with HotSpot)

original_setup.solver: HotSpot (open-source thermal simulator) [9] with comparison to fast thermal model
original_setup.optimizer: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) [7] with Random Network Distillation (RND) [8] bonus for exploration
original_setup.controller: Reinforcement Learning agent with shared CNN feature encoding, policy network, and value network for sequential chiplet placement
original_setup.benchmark: Multi-GPU System [4] - three open-source benchmarks plus five synthetic systems

thermal_observable.location: Maximum operating temperature across chiplet system
thermal_observable.aggregation: Peak temperature in steady-state thermal evaluation

physical_mismatches.reason: Fast thermal model simplifies full HotSpot thermal resistance network to linear time-invariant (LTI) system; characterizes mutual-thermal resistance via 1D table rather than full 3D transient simulation

Paper does not provide complete 3D geometry, chiplet dimensions (x_m, y_m, width_m, height_m), or individual chiplet power breakdowns for Multi-GPU System benchmark - references external source [4] without reproducing layout details
Thermal analysis performed in steady-state via self-thermal and mutual-thermal resistance tables; no transient thermal dynamics or temporal controller feedback mechanisms described

studio_assumptions: Chiplet system modeled as 2.5D integration with interposer and microbump connections
Maximum temperature serves as primary thermal constraint in reward function with temperature limitation T0 and sigmoid penalty scaling
Reward function combines wirelength W and temperature T as: R = −λ × W − µ × (max(T − T0, 0))^α / (1 + e^(−(T − T0))) where λ, µ, T0, α are hyperparameters
Fast thermal model replaces HotSpot by pre-computing self-thermal resistance table from single HotSpot run per design and characterizing mutual-thermal resistance versus distance in 1D lookup
RND exploration bonus applied during RL training to encourage novel state discovery
Sequential chiplet placement with action masking for infeasible positions
Microbump assignments optimized for minimum total wirelength post-placement before thermal evaluation
